In the fall of 2024, The Trail Conservancy held a second round of community open houses, small groups, popped up at neighborhood events, presented to neighborhood associations, and interviewed neighbors. We discussed early concept designs for the play area, trailhead, and trail enhancements originally identified in the Holly Shores/Edward Rendon Sr. Park at Festival Beach. Our team heard from 267 people in person and 356 through an online survey, with 30% of respondents from the 78702 zip code.

Help Us Design! | Open House

We are in our final phase of community engagement! We need your input to finalize and refine our concept designs for the future play area, trail enhancements, and new trailhead at Holly Shores.

Join TTC on April 12 from 9-11 AM at the Camacho Activity Center to share your thoughts and enjoy free breakfast tacos.

Can’t make it? Join us April 22 from 5:30-7:30 PM!

Wishbone Bridge & Unity Underpass Ribbon Cutting Celebration

The completion of the Wishbone Bridge marks a milestone for the Butler Trail, completing the 10-mile loop and creating a seamless, traffic-free experience for Trail users! Join The Trail Conservancy and the City of Austin on Saturday, February 7th, from 10 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. for a celebration and party on the plaza and be one of the first to enjoy the new pedestrian bridge, underpass, and benches.


Add to Calendar


RSVP Today

Getting There

There are three entrances to the Wishbone Bridge:

  • South of Longhorn Dam (entrance to the Unity Underpass)
  • North of Longhorn Dam at the end of Canterbury St. 
  • North of the Longhorn Dam at the end of the old Holly peninsula

  • Parking is available at Krieg Field (click for exact location)


About the Project

In 2018, the City of Austin’s Transportation and Public Works Department partnered with the Parks and Recreation Department and Capital Delivery Services to develop a new pedestrian and bicycle bridge over Lady Bird Lake near the Longhorn Dam. Through community engagement, a “wishbone” shaped bridge was chosen to connect the Ann and Roy Butler Trail at Longhorn Shores, Canterbury, and the Holly Peninsula in Town Lake Metropolitan Park. This project began construction in early July 2024, and the completed bridge provides an alternate option to the sidewalk on Pleasant Valley Road and fills a gap on the Butler Trail. On opening day, the bridge will also feature 14 stunning new Maraca Benches. Designed by Austin-based Lemmo Architecture and Design and fabricated by Harvest Lumber Co., these benches honor the neighborhood’s Hispanic roots, history, and culture. 

The Unity Underpass, which connects Longhorn Shores to the Roy G. Guerrero Trail and Krieg Fields, includes Austin Art in Public Places’ latest commission, Absolute Equality: Unity Tunnel by Reginald Adams. Over 200 local residents contributed to the new 130’ long public artwork featuring a mosaic installation of glass and porcelain tile, ceramic, limestone, and acrylic paint.

Merlin Tuttle Day:
Congress Ave Bat Celebration

August 26
@
5:30 pm
–
8:00 pm

Thanks to renowned bat conservationist Merlin Tuttle’s lifelong dedication, bats are now a staple of Austin’s culture. Former Austin Mayor Steve Adler officially proclaimed Merlin’s birthday, August 26th, as Merlin Tuttle Day in honor of Merlin’s success in saving the city’s now world-famous bats. And this year, we’re celebrating the addition of a new, more interactive visitor experience on the Trail: Bat City.

This collaborative effort between Merlin Tuttle’s Bat Conservation, Austin Bat Refuge, Bat Conservation International, The Trail Conservancy, and the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation is an educational experience designed to transform how visitors engage with Austin’s Congress Avenue Bridge bat colony. Through on-site signage, digital content, short-form films, and interactive learning tools, the project blends science, storytelling, and public education to deepen understanding of one of the world’s largest urban bat populations.

See the new signs and celebrate Austin’s bats: Wednesday, August 26, 5:30 – 8:00 PM.


Add to Calendar

Getting There

Parking is available in the Statesman lot or 0.5 miles west at Auditorium Shores.

About Bat City

A collaborative effort between Award-winning filmmaker Skip Hobbie, Merlin Tuttle’s Bat Conservation, Austin Bat Refuge, Bat Conservation International, The Trail Conservancy, and the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, Bat City is an educational experience designed to transform how visitors engage with Austin’s Congress Avenue Bridge bat colony.

events.title: Open House: Eastside Family Garden Design Concepts
events.description:
Eastside Family Garden Project Open House

See the future of the Trail’s Eastside! Join The Trail Conservancy at the Camacho Activity Center to see the latest design and art concepts for the Eastside Family Garden project!

  • Breakfast tacos provided
  • Meet Lys Santamaria (project artist consultant) and Edith Uresti from Rialto Studio (project landscape architect) and learn about the artistic interpretation in the project
  • See the latest project designs and art concepts

About the Project

The Eastside Family Garden will revitalize over 2 acres of neglected parkland, creating a recreational space that blends traditional playscapes, nature play, and inviting gathering areas—all purposefully designed with shade, native restoration, and water access in mind.

“The idea of home / la casa can be expressed through both form and feeling – by creating spaces that echo the comfort of domestic life and the rhythm of nature.” – Lys Santamaria, project artist

Our design reflects key themes voiced by the community, ensuring the space serves all ages and needs:

  • Multigenerational Accessibility: Play and park features designed for everyone—teens, adults, and seniors—not just young children.
  • Enhanced Shade & Comfort: A mix of shade trees and structures to provide relief from the Texas sun.
  • Ecological Restoration: Native plantings, lush grasses, and a wildflower meadow preserve the area’s natural beauty.
  • Waterfront Connection: Expanded views and access to the lagoon, fostering interaction with nature.
  • Versatile Open Lawns: Space for backyard games, outdoor programming, and camp/class staging in partnership with Camacho Activity Center and Mendez Recreation Center.
